title: Dispatch
description: The daemon's call on a module to do one system step. The file holds two documents: the request at #/definitions/request and the answer at #/definitions/answer. Dispatching again under the same dispatch id must be safe, and the module guarantees it.

request.title: Dispatch request
request.description: One system step to do. It carries ids and the step's arguments only; the module pulls everything else through the core's query API.

project.description: The project the flow run belongs to, so the module resolves the project's settings and credential profile.

parcelId.description: The parcel the flow run acts on.

flowRunId.description: The flow run the step belongs to.

step.description: The step's name, prefixed by the module's name and a slash, as describe lists it.

visit.description: Which visit to the step this is, counting from 1.

dispatchId.description: The id the daemon minted for this dispatch and recorded on the flow run before calling.

resumed.description: Whether the flow run was resumed while this visit was its current step, which is what a wait step waits for.

workPath.description: The flow run's work path, the directory a step that prepares a workspace populates.

arguments.description: The step's arguments, the JSON object the flow author wrote. It is left open here; the step's argument schema in describe governs it.

answer.title: Dispatch answer
answer.description: How the module answers a dispatch: done with a result, paused with a reason and a lever, or running.

done.description: The step finished, whatever its verdict.

paused.description: The step stopped the flow run to wait for a person.

reason.description: Why the flow run is paused, shown to a person.

lever.description: What a person acts on to resume the flow run.

running.description: The step goes on after the answer; the module records its outcome later through a core command naming the dispatch id.

result.description: The step's result document, which the flow's routes read. It carries a verdict; the rest is the step's declared result schema, so it is left open here.

verdict.description: The value the flow's routes read.
